partial.label: partial
partial.blurb: present but narrower than the rubric asks

halves.label: The learning half
halves.blurb: How a version gets better without getting worse.

halves.label: The operating half
halves.blurb: What happens once it is live, and who finds out first.

rows.label: Evals & golden set
rows.question: Is there a versioned golden set, and can anyone reproduce the score offline?
rows.how: Committed manifest — train 100 / gate 100 reports (368 / 349 questions), seed 2026, drawn only from conversations GEPA and s7 never saw — plus committed prediction CSVs for every run of both runtimes. Each turn carries numeric and program match, a cascade flag and a gold-derived per-agent panel.

rows.label: LLM-as-judge
rows.question: Who grades the open-ended answers, and is the judge independent of the model being graded?
rows.how: Tried last (s12/s13): a Haiku 4.5 judge that never sees gold reads each finished turn's trace and returns a band from six named checks. Scored once on the sealed gate split — high band 91.46% against 90.54% releasing everything, a 95% interval of 87.9–95.2% that contains the baseline, 6 of 33 failures caught at the cost of 27 correct answers withheld. Not adopted as a gate; the band ships as an advisory caution (JUDGE_MODE=advisory).

rows.label: Regression gate
rows.question: What stops a worse version from shipping?
rows.how: Net positive on the fixed unseen split and one-sided cluster-corrected McNemar p < 0.05, with a bootstrap CI on every verdict; --promote refused on train evidence. Three earlier promotions rolled back under it; v8 is the first that passed. CI re-scores the champion from its CSV on every PR — but v8's registry metrics are empty, so that floor is −0.5% and cannot fail. Open defect.

rows.label: Learning loop
rows.question: How does the system get better — and is each change traceable to one lever?
rows.how: A teacher on Opus 5 blames one agent per first-wrong turn; the challenger rewrites only that prompt; a campaign is up to five experiments, target rotated off after two rejections. Three campaigns, seven experiments, one promotion (v8). The runtime arm promoted sdk_v1 to sdk_champion and rejected sdk_v2. Holdout release gate built, never opened.

rows.label: Guardrails & security
rows.question: What sits between the model and anything it can touch — data, tools, money, other users?
rows.how: Abuse controls, not policy gates: one LLM choke point owns the demo gate, retries and the 120 s ceiling; an in-flight cap of 4 and a per-IP window of 30 / 60 s; admin writes need the owner token and a non-demo build; replay declines below its match threshold. No per-user auth, no row-level policy, no red-team suite.

rows.label: Observability & tracing
rows.question: Can you replay exactly what the agent did on one request, and see the fleet's health on one screen?
rows.how: Every pipeline LLM call is an MLflow span linked to its run; SDK spans opened by hand at one chokepoint. Every served turn is a row at /admin/traces with per-stage IO, tokens, latency and bundle id. GET /metrics/production splits by source and never blends. The demo container has no tracking server.

rows.label: Cost tracking & control
rows.question: What does one answer cost, what caps the worst day, and what's the cheap-by-default tier?
rows.how: Per-turn cost from the runner's own metrics, prices declared in code; the SDK arm's spend recorded per question. A gate pass is ~$1–2 on the pipeline, $27.62 on the Sonnet 5 session and $17.14 on Haiku 4.5. The public deployment performs no inference.

rows.label: Deploy & release
rows.question: Is a merge a deploy — and does the deploy prove the live URL is what it claims?
rows.how: Merge → CI → OIDC deploy to ECR and App Runner, no stored keys; the smoke test asserts mode=demo, served bundle == champion, the evidence, and a 403 on a write. Rollback is retagging a :sha. The holdout release gate is stub-tested, not exercised.

rows.label: Scale path
rows.question: What's the topology today, what's been measured under load, and what changes at 100 / 1,000 concurrent users?
rows.how: Rung 10 only. One instance, --workers 1, sessions and rate-limit state in process memory — and the code names that as the seam. No auto-scaling asserted, no load test; rungs 100 and 1,000 are design only.
